questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

The chairman's speech was _______ to the occasion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'appropriate'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** 

__
 
• In the given sentence the word **appropriate **is an **adjective **that expresses an **opinion **on the speech.
 
• it is followed by the** infinitive to **as given in the sentence.
 
• In this case, the **infinitive 'to'** extends the meaning( to give an **opinion **on the speech) and completes the sentence.

**Hence, the correct sentence is**__: *The chairman's speech was **appropriate **to the occasion*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the meaning of the given options as well so there is no confusion regarding the word choice.
 
• **appropriate**: suitable or proper in the circumstance
 
• **right**: morally good, justified or acceptable
 
• **correct**: free from error
 
• **useful**: able to be used in a practical purpose in several ways

So, from the given options '**appropriate**' is the correct word choice.

 
• Example: *Her dress was not **appropriate **for the occasion*.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

If you had exercise regularly, you would have been fit today.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'exercise regularly'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** 

__
 
• The aforementioned sentence is in **past tense **and we can notice the word '**had**' before the error.
 
• This implies that we need to use **past participle **in the sentence.
 
• We can change the form of the verb into a past participle by adding -**ed **to the verb.
 
• The correct verb form is **exercised regularly**

**Hence, the correct sentence is**:__ *If you had __**exercised regularly**__, you would have been fit today*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **__Hint__**

__
 
• Notice if there are auxiliary verbs such as has, have, or had before the erroneous part.
 
• Generally, the past participle will be used with auxiliary verbs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A verb can be changed into past tense by adding** d,ed, or t.**
 
• Example:
 
 
• work to worked(**ed**)
 
• dance to danced(**d**)
 
• deal to dealt(**t**)

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Mr. Roy was not only very successful and humble also.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'and humble also'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of **correlative conjunction** since it has **not only** in the first clause.
 
• Correlative conjunctions are a **pair of words **that connect **similar entities**(nouns, adjectives, etc) in the sentence **together**.
 
• It is used to put emphasis on certain elements.
 
• Common examples of correlative conjunctions include **either or, neither nor, not only but also, both and**.

**Hence the correct sentence is**__: *Mr. Roy was not only very successful __**but also **__humble*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Correlative conjunction is also known to maintain the grammatical balance in a sentence.
 
• it can only connect two similar entities together. Like if the first clause of the sentence had a noun then it will be connected to another noun in the second clause of the sentence.
 
 
• Example: **Both** India **and **China have huge populations. (**nouns**)
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• It is really easy to get confused about which conjunction to use in a particular sentence.
 
• If the first clause of the statement is similar to the second clause then we can use coordinating conjunction like **and**.
 
 
• **Example**: *He was handsome **and **talented as well*.
 
 
 
• If the first clause of the statement is in stark contrast to the second clause of the statement then we use **but.**
 
 
• **Example: ***He was talented **but **lacked discipline.*
 
 
 
• There is no need to use commas in case two nouns are connected through conjunction but in other sentences a comma is necessary.
 
 
• **Example**: The restaurant owner not only offered us a free lunch, but he also gave us a complimentary beverage.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

These dates are from Dubai, __isn't it__?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**aren't they**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This sentence is an example of a **tag question**.
 
• Question tags are always placed at the end.
 
• A **positive **statement is followed by a **negative** question** **tag.
 
• A **negative **statement is followed by a **positive **question tag.
 
• The auxiliary verb used in the question tag is according to the statement.
 
• In the given sentence, the correct form of the question tag should be "aren't they" as the **subject**(dates) is **plural.**

**Hence, the correct sentence is**__: These dates are from Dubai, *__**aren't they**__*?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Contractions are words formed by shortening the words by omitting some letters.
 
• Words like **isn't it, aren't they, could've, and would've** are also known as **contractions**.
 
• Isn't: It is contracted form of "is not"; aren't: are not.
 
• If the subject is **singular**, we use the contraction **isn't it?**
 
• Question tags are always separated from the statement by a **comma**.
 
• **Example**:* It's a pleasant day to play golf, **isn't it__**?*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

He was _______ to six months of imprisonment for stealing.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**condemned**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The most appropriate word to fill in the blank is "condemned."

__
 
• Option 3, "condemned," means to express strong disapproval of or to sentence someone to a particular punishment. In the given sentence, the person was sentenced to six months of imprisonment for stealing. Hence, the correct option is 3) condemned.
 
• The other options are not fitting for the given sentence. Option 1, "conformed," means to comply with rules or standards, which does not make sense in the context of the sentence. Option 2, "convinced," means to persuade someone to do or believe something, which is not appropriate in the given context. Option 4, "contacted," means to communicate with someone, which is also not appropriate in this context.

**Hence, the correct sentence is:**__ *He was __condemned__ to six months of imprisonment for stealing.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** *

__
 
• In the given sentence, the person is being punished for stealing. The correct word to use in the blank would be a verb that indicates the action of punishing someone for a crime.
 
• The first option, "conformed," is not appropriate in this context. Conforming means to comply with rules or standards, but it does not indicate punishment.
 
• The second option, "convinced," is also not fitting in the context of the sentence. Convincing means to persuade someone to do or believe something, which is not related to the punishment for a crime.
 
• The fourth option, "contacted," is not appropriate in this context either. Contacting means to communicate with someone, which is not related to the punishment for a crime.
 
• The third option, "condemned," is the most appropriate word to use in this sentence. Condemning means to express strong disapproval of or to sentence someone to a particular punishment, which is what happened in this sentence. The person was sentenced to six months of imprisonment for stealing, which is a form of punishment. Therefore, "condemned" is the correct word to fill in the blank.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] 

**Hinglish__**

• शब्दों का अर्थ
 
• **confirmed**: पक्का
 
• **convinced**: कायल
 
• **condemned**: निंदा की
 
• **contacted**: संपर्क
 
• **Example**:* Loud music at night was **condemned **__by the hostel warden.*
